name: @draggable/storeshot-mcp

tools.name: get_store_requirements
tools.description:
Returns the screenshot rules of the App Store and/or Google Play: device classes (required, conditional or optional), how many screenshots each needs, accepted sizes and formats, and the Google Play feature graphic.
When to use: first, before planning a listing, to know which devices a store requires. Then list_devices for exact ids and create_screenshot_set to make everything.
Credits: free, no credits.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description:
Lists the output sizes (device ids) Storeshot can generate for the App Store and Google Play: id, store, kind (screenshot or feature_graphic), pixel size and orientations.
When to use: to pick valid `device` values for generate_screenshot or `devices` for create_screenshot_set. Use get_store_requirements to learn which sizes a store requires.
Credits: free, no credits.
Deprecated sizes are hidden unless includeDeprecated is true; replacedBy names their replacement.

tools.name: upload_screenshot
tools.description:
Uploads one raw app screenshot from a local file (PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 20 MiB) and returns its uploadId.
When to use: once per raw screenshot before create_screenshot_set or generate_screenshot (both also accept { path } and upload for you). Only image files are sent; anything else is refused before upload.
Credits: free, no credits. Uploads count towards the account upload quota and are deleted after 30 days.

path.description: Absolute path of a local PNG, JPEG or WebP file.

tools.name: generate_screenshot
tools.description:
Turns one raw screenshot into one marketing image for one store size (a list_devices id), with an optional caption, palette and logo.
When to use: for a single image or a quick try. For a whole listing (every screen on every required device, one charge) use create_screenshot_set instead.
Credits: 1 credit with a live key (ss_live_…), charged when the job is created and refunded automatically if it fails or is canceled before it starts. Test keys (ss_test_…) never spend credits and return sample images of the exact size.
Returns the job id at once; pass waitSeconds to wait, or follow it with get_job_status, then download_results.

path.description: Absolute path of a local PNG, JPEG or WebP file.

device.description: A list_devices id of the same store.

path.description: Absolute path of a local PNG, JPEG or WebP file.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the first job instead of creating another.

waitSeconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to finish (0 = return at once). Most clients time out a tool call after about 60 s unless they reset on progress: prefer 50 or less and call get_job_status again.

tools.name: create_screenshot_set
tools.description:
Makes a whole store listing in one job: every screen (1–10 raw screenshots, one caption each) on every device of one or both stores, plus an optional Google Play feature graphic, with one palette and logo for all. Without devices a store gets the sizes it requires.
When to use: to produce or refresh App Store / Google Play screenshots. With a live key call it first with dryRun: true to see the cost. Then get_job_status and download_results (layout "fastlane" for fastlane projects).
Credits: 1 credit per image with a live key: screens × devices, +1 per feature graphic, all charged at create or none (INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS). dryRun: true quotes for free. Failed or canceled images are refunded. Test keys (ss_test_…) never spend credits and return sample images of the exact size.
At most 50 images per set. Screens accept { uploadId } or { path } (uploaded first, also for dryRun).

path.description: Absolute path of a local PNG, JPEG or WebP file.

devices.description: list_devices ids of this store, at most one per device class. Absent: the store defaults.

path.description: Absolute path of a local PNG, JPEG or WebP file.

dryRun.description: Quote only: validates and returns the cost; nothing is created or charged.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the first job instead of creating another.

waitSeconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to finish (0 = return at once). Most clients time out a tool call after about 60 s unless they reset on progress: prefer 50 or less and call get_job_status again.

tools.name: get_job_status
tools.description:
Returns the status of a generation or a screenshot set by id: status, final, image counts, credits charged and refunded, result URLs (signed, they expire after 15 minutes) and per-image errors.
When to use: after generate_screenshot or create_screenshot_set, until final is true; then download_results. Pass waitSeconds to wait here (progress notifications are sent when your client asks for them).
Credits: free, no credits.

kind.description: Absent: looked up as a set, then as a generation.

waitSeconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to finish (0 = return at once). Most clients time out a tool call after about 60 s unless they reset on progress: prefer 50 or less and call get_job_status again.

tools.name: download_results
tools.description:
Saves the finished images of a screenshot set (or of one generation) into a local folder and returns the absolute file paths. Sets: layout "store" (<store>/<device>/NN.png) or "fastlane" (fastlane/screenshots/en-US/… and fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/…; pass the project root as folder).
When to use: once get_job_status says final (or to save what succeeded so far: complete tells you). Existing files are never replaced unless overwrite is true; files of an earlier download that this one lacks are left in place. Nothing is written outside the folder, and never through symbolic links.
Credits: free, no credits.

folder.description: Absolute path of the folder to write into (created if missing).

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description:
Returns the account credit balance: total and the starter, subscription and purchased parts, and the environment (test or live) of the key in use.
When to use: before create_screenshot_set or generate_screenshot with a live key, or after a 402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS. Test keys never spend credits.
Credits: free, no credits.

tools.name: link_status
tools.description:
Reports whether this server has a Storeshot API key: linked (and where it came from), pending (with the link and code to show the user), expired, denied, failed or not started.
When to use: after another tool answered ACCOUNT_LINK_REQUIRED or ACCOUNT_LINK_PENDING, to check whether the user approved. It never starts linking itself and needs no key.
Credits: free, no credits.

instructions:
Storeshot turns raw app screenshots into App Store and Google Play marketing images.
Typical flow: get_store_requirements, then upload_screenshot for each raw screenshot, then create_screenshot_set (with a live key call it with dryRun: true first to see the cost), then get_job_status with waitSeconds until final, then download_results (layout "fastlane" into the project root for fastlane projects).
Test keys (ss_test_…) are free and return sample images of the exact sizes; live keys (ss_live_…) make real images and spend credits. If a tool answers ACCOUNT_LINK_REQUIRED, show the user the link and code, then call link_status.
Never ask the user to paste an API key into the chat.
